newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - June 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - June 16.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

The OECD's latest forecasts for industrialised nations say the world economy is enjoying its most widespread and strongest growth since 1989, with a predicted average growth of three percent in 1997 and 2.7 percent in 1998. Australia is tipped to achieve growth of 3.5 percent for this year and next. Page 1.

There are strong signals that there will be a major change in direction for Optus Communications' when the board meets on June 26 to consider the future of the company's broadband cable business and pay-TV interests. A strategic shift is likely to see the loss-making pay-TV operation sold to re-establish the company as a specialist telecommunications carrier. Page 1.

Under proposals to be released today as part of the ongoing project to rewrite and simplify the Income Tax Assessment Act, the Australian Taxation Office is set to introduce a sweeping overhaul of the capital gains tax rules, but the tax industry is
disapointed saying there is little in the way of substantial reform. Page 3.

The Transport Workers Union's campaign to win a pay increase on the ground, which was rejected by the Australian Industrial Relations Commission, will see trucking companies that refuse to pay an 11 per cent wage rise facing black bans from today on the loading and unloading of trucks operated by the company. Page 3.
THE AUSTRALIAN

The Federal Government yesterday revealed two more MPs are under police investigation over allegations of rorting expenses. The Government has refused to name the MPs, but the allegations are believed to concern travel allowances and travel-related expenss. Page 1.

The discovery of 139 expensively dressed Chinese in a well-equipped, steel-hulled boat entering Australian waters has fuelled Federal Government fears over the increasingly sophisticated operations used to bring illegal immigrants to the country. Page 1.

Angus and Robertson will publish a new series of May Gibbs' classic Snugglepot and Cuddlepie with redrawn colour pictures and a shortened story in an effort to appeal to a new generation of readers. Although the stories are being reproduced with the permision of the May Gibbs Estate, the decision has reignited debate about the ethics of tampering with dead authors' works. Page 1.

The controversial work-for-the-dole scheme could trigger a double dissolution with the Federal Government planing to reject the Senate's amendments to the legislation. Special reports to be released today by the ALP and Democrats will make it clear the Parties intend to reject a compulsory element to the program. Page 1.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Jesse Hurley of Erina on the Central Coast celebrated her 107th birthday yesterday, happily recieving a third telegram from the Queen to add to those she got on her 100th and 105th birthdays. Hurley is the second-oldest woman in Australia. Page 1.

Prime Minister John Howard and Federal Treasurer Peter Costello will tonight launch a push for tax reform which is likely to include a goods and services tax.. They will seek support for the tax reform by emphasising the failures of the current tax base. age 1.

The NSW Government has warned that teachers moving from interstate will be banned from working in the State's public schools unless the other States adopt new guidelines to identify those teachers found to have been involved in improper sexual conduct with students. Page 2.

Federal Science and Technology Minister Peter McGuaran has welcomed the latest AGB McNair opinion poll which found that Australians are more interested in news on science, technology, medical breakthroughs and pollution than sport, politics,
employment an crime. Page 3.
THE AGE

Victorian magistrates have condemned the conditions in some suburban police stations and complained to the State government saying some prison cells are infested with lice and fleas, have no natural light, and are dank. Inmates sometimes remain locked in for up to 20 hours with no exercise, and defendants accused of minor offences mix with defendants accused of serious offences such as murder and armed robbery. Page 1.

Police are investigating yesterday's disappearance of Jaidyn Leski, a 14-month-old boy, from a couch in the lounge room of a Newborough house in eastern Victoria. Leski was left sleeping on the couch while his mother's boyfriend left to pick up his mother, but when they returned one hour later Jaidyn was gone, two front windows were smashed and a pig's head was dumped in the front yard. Page 1.

Deputy Prime Minister Tim Fischer yesterday said the Federal Government would send a message to Asia that immigrants seeking residence in Australia must use the system. The announcement comes after the arrival of 140 Asians in the Torres Strait on Friday amid concerns of an immigration racket. Page 3.

The Federal Opposition employment spokesperson, Martin Ferguson, yesterday foreshadowed Labor amendments to key employment service reforms to ensure all employers and workers retain access to free and high-quality employment services, and to ensure that all new agencies are registered and accredited.
Page 2.
